definition: Training an AI agent within a simulated environment rather than the real world, allowing for faster, cheaper, and safer iteration.
details: Simulation-based training is widely used in robotics and reinforcement learning research, since it allows generating vast amounts of experience quickly and safely testing behaviors that would be risky or costly in the real world.
story: Think of a hiker descending a foggy hill in the dark, taking small steps and feeling for the steepest way down. The machine starts out clumsy, makes mistakes, and is nudged a little less wrong every time. It is the same loop you use to learn anything: try, miss, correct, try again. Skill, for a model, is just error pushed down until it is small enough to ignore. And that is Simulation-Based Training — the quiet loop that turns flailing into skill.
